student_notes: Questions from production engineer review. Focus on practical application.

questions.question: You are building an AI agent for an e-commerce site. A user says 'add the blue shirt to my cart'. Your pipeline classifies this as intent=add_to_cart and the action executes successfully. What tier does this belong to and why?
options: A. Tier 3a — it uses the LLM to understand 'blue shirt'
B. Tier 1 — the orchestrator executes the action directly with zero LLM cost
C. Tier 2 — the orchestrator fetches the cart state and returns a template
D. Tier 0 — authentication is required before cart operations
questions.explanation: Tier 1 is for direct orchestrator-executed actions. The SLM has already classified the intent and extracted the entity ('blue shirt' → product_id from carousel_state or entity resolution). The orchestrator calls addToCart(product_id) and returns a success template. No LLM is involved. This is the critical design principle: the LLM is the last resort. If the orchestrator can complete the action deterministically, it should.

questions.question: The course says 'the LLM is about 15% of this codebase'. Identify three specific system components that make up the other 85% and explain what would break if each one were removed.
questions.answer: Sample answer: (1) The asyncio.Queue/SSE streaming infrastructure — without it, LLM output cannot reach the browser in real-time; users would see blank screens until the full response completed. (2) The Redis session store — without it, every turn is stateless; 'show me 2BHK instead' cannot change a previous filter because there are no previous filters to change. (3) The safety_node/validate_slm_node guardrails — without them, prompt injection attacks bypass classification, and malformed SLM JSON crashes downstream nodes.
questions.explanation: The point is that the value of an AI agent is in the surrounding system, not the model. Students who think AI agents are just 'ChatGPT with a system prompt' will build brittle systems that work in demos but fail in production.

questions.question: A user asks 'show me properties in Bandra under 2Cr' then immediately says 'actually make it 3BHK'. The SLM output for the second message has filter_delta: {'bhk': [3]} and pivot: false. After filter_apply_node runs, what does session.active_filters contain?
options: D. The filter_delta is rejected because pivot=false and no city context
questions.explanation: filter_apply_node merges filter_delta into the existing session.active_filters. Since pivot=false, sanitize_node does not clear any existing keys. The REPLACE semantics apply: bhk is replaced with [3]. All other keys (localities, price_max, city) persist from the previous turn. This is the multi-turn conversation memory working correctly.
